description: Ocean surface wind refers to the wind velocity measured or derived at approximately 10 meters above the sea surface. These winds are a critical component of air-sea interaction, driving ocean circulation, wave generation, heat and gas exchange, and influencing sea ice dynamics in polar regions. Ocean surface winds are measured by satellite scatterometers, radiometers, and altimeters, as well as in-situ instruments on ships and buoys. In the Southern Ocean, surface winds, particularly the strong westerlies, play a key role in driving the Antarctic Circumpolar Current and modulating sea ice extent.
title: Ocean Surface Wind
